summary: embed.Embedder gains Identity() and Limits(); the Bedrock client keeps today's behaviour, identity us.cohere.embed-v4:0 and its own 96/200k/throttle codes; a new net/http Azure client posts the route INFRA-399 proves (documented: {endpoint}/embeddings?api-version=2024-05-01-preview with input_type and dimensions 1536), key or keyless (hand-written Entra exchange of a projected token), identity azure:<host>/<deployment>. Settings DISPATCH_EMBEDDER and DISPATCH_AZURE_*; search filters e.model = identity; embedqueue.Run runs a no-lease coverage pass (insert missing, CAS-repair stale, drop other identity's vectors, re-admit other identity's dead rows) at start and every 10 min; backfill-embeddings and its checkpoint table go; migrations add pending_since and dead_model; GET /api/v1/search/coverage reports per kind and total; gcp:Dispatch gains Azure inputs and issuer/subject outputs. Live Azure proof runs against INFRA-399's deployment.

findings.finding: F1: Azure route is deprecated, 512-token vs 128k contradiction, no Azure batch value; a 1536-wide answer alone proves neither input_type nor no truncation.
findings.answer: INFRA-399 settles route, input limit and keyless by live calls; T8 adjusts the client to them; the live proof table checks document vs query vectors differ and a 32,000-character body's vector differs from its head-only vector, with negative controls; a real 512-token limit goes to the architect, no chunking (architect, 2026-10-25).

findings.finding: F2: rolling deploy with old readers/workers or two differently configured processes.
findings.answer: Decision 8: new search filters by identity; the periodic pass drops another identity's vectors, so an old process's commits are re-embedded and the state converges after it exits; one deployment runs one configuration (stated in the guide); T4 tests a second Deps with another identity committing after the pass.

findings.finding: F3: INFRA-156 PR7 retires whole-text kinds; coverage, invalidation, report and tests must follow whichever merges second; INFRA-156's plan assumes a lease.
findings.answer: Decision 13: coverageSources is the one list; if PR7 is on main, it takes PR7's grain and never re-creates retired rows; otherwise PR7 carries it. The architect accepted no lease and was told of INFRA-156's note.

findings.finding: F4: repairing a mismatched row with embeddings_enqueue semantics can clobber a fresher trigger write.
findings.answer: Decision 8: missing rows insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; stale rows use a compare-and-swap update guarded by the row's content_hash captured in the CTE, re-checked on the latest version; T4 has a deterministic interleaving test.

findings.finding: F5: coverage text and hash must be trigger-exact, or rows flip and retries reset.
findings.answer: Decision 9 lists each kind's exact FROM, id, text and write time from 0073-0077 and the 0072 hash; T4 parity test: two passes and a non-text update change nothing and call the embedder zero times.

findings.finding: F6: idempotence and two-process safety of the invalidation are unspecified; dead-row handling.
findings.answer: Decision 8: one transition per row (embedding/model/embedded_hash nulled, so the row leaves the predicate); pending rows keep claim, backoff and pending_since; skip locked; dead rows re-admitted only when dead_model differs from the identity, recorded by retryRows; T4 runs two passes concurrently.

findings.finding: F7: dropping embeddings_backfill_progress vs expand/contract; pending_since defaults for old producers; census.
findings.answer: Decision 10: pending_since has default now(), old inserts go through the replaced embeddings_enqueue or the default; the drop is justified because no server of the old release reads the table (only the person-run old subcommand), named in the PR; each migration has its census; T3 tests old-style inserts.

findings.finding: F8: the model filter's HNSW plan and recall with a large foreign share; the index test uses copied SQL.
findings.answer: Decision 7: foreign vectors are nulled, leaving the HNSW partial index, so the filter only catches roll-time writes; T5 makes the index test run the five real candidate statements with $11 bound.

findings.finding: F9: identity encoding, place vs model, WithModel provenance bug.
findings.answer: Decisions 2-3: Bedrock records its configured model id (unchanged value, fixes the queue.go:609 bug); Azure records azure:<host>/<deployment>; the architect accepted that the place belongs in the identity; a model change on Azure needs a new deployment name, stated in the guide.

findings.finding: F10: report definitions: current needs a non-null vector, age for absent rows, nil embedder, one snapshot.
findings.answer: Decision 11, agreed with INFRA-194's planner: one statement; current = row, non-null vector, identity, hash of current text; failed = dead and not current; age from pending_since or the content's write time, null when none; identity null with no embedder; T5 covers each state.

findings.finding: F11: keyless premise unverified, live surface circular with INFRA-394.
findings.answer: The architect split the Azure side into INFRA-399, which declares the deployment and federated identity and proves keyless from a projected token; T8 runs the live proof there, reports a missing surface and waits for the architect's go.

findings.finding: F12: no command per acceptance line.
findings.answer: The plan's proof table names surface, command, observed result and negative control for each of the eight lines; static checks are CI's; root A1-A3 are INFRA-394's, A4 is T1/T4/T5 tests.

findings.finding: F13: settings reader tests, _FILE semantics, Pulumi unknown inputs, cmd/dispatch/AGENTS.md.
findings.answer: T2 adds reader cases, _FILE precedence and blank-file refusals; T6 tests unknown and resource-output inputs; T7 updates cmd/dispatch/AGENTS.md.

findings.finding: F14: public-repo text rules and private evidence storage.
findings.answer: The proof section keeps raw output under $TMPDIR/infra393-proof and public text to keys, counts, ranks, dates and SHAs; this PR needs no search query text (root A2 belongs to INFRA-394).

specDepartures.spec: Keyless sign-in to Azure with Dispatch's own Google identity is preferred where the plan finds it works.
specDepartures.plan: Keyless sign-in uses a Kubernetes projected service-account token for Dispatch's service account, issued by the GKE dispatch cluster's OIDC issuer, exchanged at Entra through a federated credential (as INFRA-399 declares), not a Google-signed ID token.
specDepartures.evidence: Dispatch is a direct Workload Identity principal with no Google service account (packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch_cloud.go:163-172); Google's ID-token flow is documented for a resource that can have a service account attached (cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/get-id-token). INFRA-399's spec proves keyless from a projected token.
